thread:
jane: Quick question — proposal to add a top-level field `response_schema_version` to /v1/generate responses. Is this considered a breaking change for clients that parse output?
ben: Short answer: depends. If it's optional and defaults to existing behaviour, not strictly breaking. But some strict parsers might fail if they do schema validation. :thinking_face:
alex: Do we have clients that do strict JSON schema validation today? I think some partners do for enterprise integrations.
sam: We should assume at least 2 customers use strict validators. We should either make it an opt-in header or add it behind a feature flag for a rollout window.
priya: For Dedicated customers we already let them pin model versions — they might expect stable response shape. Any change needs a clear deprecation timeline.
marta: Ops note: deploy-bot shows canary passed for the generator change branch: https://ci.internal/runs/98765 :white_check_mark:
ben: Proposal: add header negotiation first — e.g. client can send `X-Redwood-Accept-Schema-Version: 2` and server adds `response_schema_version` when header present. That avoids breaking old parsers.
jane: That sounds reasonable. If header absent, keep current shape. We still need a long-lived plan for announcing v2 of the schema and eventual default switch.
alex: Timeline suggestion: announce 8 weeks before turning it on by default, 4 weeks for partner previews. Docs + sample client code + migration guide.
sam: Also add automated.integration tests: run schema validation against our internal test-suite and a sample pinned-client run to catch regressions.
priya: Can we tie the rollout to model pinning state? Like only enable schema v2 for requests pinned to model x.y or for hosted-only first.
ben: Yep, smart routing can gate by model version or by customer tier. Recommend hosted -> dedicated -> private in that order.
jane: Who wants to own the comms and customer-facing migration notes? I can draft the engineering-side RFC and changelog entries.
marta: I can coordinate with support and send a short customer note template once RFC is ready.
priya: I'll reach out to the top 3 customers that have strict validators and offer a preview.
alex: I'll add a short compatibility test in the API contract CI that asserts absence/presence rules for `response_schema_version` depending on the header. Example snippet: ```bash
# simulate header negotiation
curl -H "X-Redwood-Accept-Schema-Version: 2" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' | jq '.response_schema_version'
```
ben: For changelog language: call it "schema opt-in field" and avoid saying "breaking" until after preview. Also include rollback playbook steps.
jane: Action items: 1) I will open RFC w/ sample responses + migration checklist (due EOD tomorrow). 2) alex add CI test (PR by Fri). 3) priya run customer outreach (start next week). 4) marta prepare support template.
sam: +1. Add a short eval harness to Redwood Optimize to measure any token delta or latency impact.
deploy-bot: CI: schema-negotiation-tests: passed (job 372) — canary green.
ben: Thanks everyone. If no objections I'll proceed with header-based rollout plan and draft deprecation timeline for the RFC. :thumbsup:
jane: No objections here. I'll cc product and legal in the RFC for compliance checks.
(End of thread)
